draft.title: How world views shape management
card: A world view affects how people judge a change to the environment. Two people can see the same change and disagree about whether it is a problem.
A person with a human-centred view may see a change as a problem when it reduces what nature gives people, such as farmland, water or income.
A person with an earth-centred view may see a change as a problem when it harms living things or places, even if people lose nothing.
World views also affect which ways of managing a change people support. Someone may back a plan that protects people's uses of land, while another backs a plan that leaves a place untouched.
draft.remember: What people see as a problem, and how they want it managed, depends on their world view.

a.q: Why might two people disagree about whether clearing bushland for a new suburb is a problem?
opts: They hold different world views about the value of nature
One of them has misread the facts about the clearing
Only people living nearby can judge an environmental change
Clearing bushland is a problem only for scientists to judge
a.why: World views shape what people value, so they can judge the same change differently. Misreading the facts is tempting, but people can agree on the facts and still disagree because of what they value.
a.clue: Think about what each person values most about the bushland.

b.q: Weeds are spreading in a reserve near Alice Springs, and no farms or visitors are affected. Which person is most likely to see this as a problem?
opts: Ben, who believes native plants have worth in themselves
Cara, who values land only for the crops it can grow
Dev, who values land only for the profit it can earn
Elly, who thinks nature matters only if people use it
b.why: Ben has an earth-centred view, so harm to native plants is a problem to him even when no people lose out. The others value land for what it gives people, and in this case people lose nothing, so they are less likely to see a problem.
b.clue: Nobody loses anything useful here, so who would still care?

a.best: They hold different world views about the value of nature

b.best: Ben, who believes native plants have worth in themselves

problems.detail: The three wrong options all say 'only' (nature matters only if people use it, land only for crops, land only for profit), while Ben's is the only option without it. A student could pick Ben from that pattern alone, without knowing the idea.
Two distractors rest on 'only' ('Only people living nearby…', '…only for scientists to judge'). This marks them as wrong and makes the right option easier to spot without knowing the idea.

'depends on their world view' suggests world view alone decides what people see as a problem. The card says a world view 'affects' how people judge a change and 'may' lead them to see a problem. 'is shaped by' or 'is affected by' would match the card.
